name: Il San Pietro di Positano
positioning: Family-run hotel carved into the cliffs outside Positano on the Amalfi Coast, with a private beach club reached by an elevator through the cliff
best_for: Couples wanting a sea-view terrace room on the Amalfi Coast
Travelers who want a private beach club, a seaside tennis court and boat outings without leaving the hotel

facts.text: Il San Pietro di Positano is set into the cliffside on the Amalfi Coast.
Rooms feature hand-painted ceramic tiles, custom-made furniture and fine Italian textiles.
Classic rooms have a private terrace overlooking the sea.
The Prestige rooms with a Positano view have large furnished terraces overlooking the town of Positano and the islands of Li Galli and Capri.
The Virginia suite occupies an entire floor, with a privileged entrance to the swimming pool and direct lift access.
The Signature rooms were designed by Fausta Gaetani.
Guests can charter the hotel's private yachts, The Dreamer and The Joey II, to explore the Amalfi Coast, Capri, Ischia and the Gulf of Naples.
The hotel's organic gardens span ten cascading terraces and supply vegetables, herbs and citrus.
Zass restaurant has panoramic sea views.
Conde Nast Traveler reports that founder Carlino Cinque opened the hotel in 1970 and it has never left the family since.
Conde Nast Traveler mentions La Prairie treatments at the spa.
Conde Nast Traveler lists a small gym with sea views and yoga and Pilates classes.

highlights.text: An elevator cut into the cliff runs from the lobby straight to the beach club.
The beach club is a private beach in a natural cove with clear Mediterranean waters.
The regulation-size tennis court sits between the rock face and a pebble beach by the sea.
The rooms are carved into the cliff overlooking the Mediterranean Sea.
The swimming pool is set on a terrace overlooking the sea and the coastal village of Praiano.

considerations.text: Conde Nast Traveler places the hotel about a mile down the coast from the center of Positano.
Conde Nast Traveler reports the hotel has an age limit for children, with ages 10 and up allowed.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the ultra-luxury positioning.
